summary: Feed s138_double is degraded: 63.8% of traffic remains ERSPAN-encapsulated and 50% of packets are missing required VLAN 20, preventing APM from parsing application flows and segment context.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags - required VLAN 20 not seen and 50% of packets arrive untagged, likely due to broker VLAN stripping policy or SPAN port configured to remove tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM loses tenant/tier segmentation for VLAN 20; cannot filter, baseline, or correlate performance by VLAN, reducing detection coverage for apps on VLAN 20 and causing incomplete transaction visibility.

recommended_fix.why: Restore and preserve 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10 and 20 through the packet broker to the APM so it can segment and monitor correctly.

findings.root_cause: Traffic is forwarded via ERSPAN without decapsulation - 1305 of 2047 frames (63.8%) still encapsulated, indicating packet broker is mirroring ERSPAN to tool port without stripping header.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees outer ERSPAN/GRE headers instead of inner application packets; cannot parse L4-L7 headers, measure latency, or decode transactions, effectively blind to 63.8% of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN encapsulation and forward only inner original packets so APM can analyze application performance.
